text:
Alex: CI alert from nightly bench — synthetic harness shows a ~7% median latency regression for seq=512 compared to baseline. p95/p99 up too. Dashboard: https://dash.redwood/internal/bench/nightly/1785. Snapshot attached. Can someone triage?

bench-bot: benchmark-ci detected deviation: synthetic/seq512 median +7%, p99 +12%. Threshold exceeded for nightly-run-1785. auto-opened ticket #INF-879.

Maya: is this just synthetic traffic or do replay runs show the same?

Alex: Synthetic definitely shows reg. Replay harness (sampled customer traces) mostly flat on median but I'm seeing intermittent tail spikes in the replay logs around the same timeframe. Suspect kernel selection + batching interplay.

Ravi: flagging PRs touching kernel selector and batching: PR#3421 (kernel selector weights) and PR#3437 (batching heuristic tweak). Any recent KV cache changes?

Sandeep: KV cache eviction tweak in PR#3418 changed early eviction threshold for interleaved sessions — could cause extra cold KV lookups for replay patterns. Might not affect strictly synthetic steady streams.

Jen: can we get a quick profiler diff? Alex, can you paste the flame lines you saw?

Alex: paste below — these are aggregated samples from perf-run. Notice the uptick in matmul kernel hot time after the selector tweak:

```
profiler-summary: seq=512, model=redwood-v1-large
aggregate: CPU samples
  matmul_kernel_v2: 38.9%  <-- up from 29.1% baseline
  attention_kv_copy: 12.2%
  kv_cache_lookup: 8.1%
  batching_dispatch: 6.3%
  scheduler_overhead: 2.0%
```

Alex: Also saw more instances where the runtime chose matmul_kernel_v2 (optimized for large batch heavy) vs matmul_kernel_fast (better for small batches). That lines up with the altered kernel priority in 3421.

Kai: my hunch: batching heuristic is producing larger transient batches on synthetic that trigger the different kernel path; for replay, interleaving + KV cache evictions create spikes. Try pinning max_batch_size=16 and rerun synthetic + replay to compare.

Maya: good call. I'll run replay harness with pinned batch size and seed for reproducibility. Command: `./tools/replay-harness --trace-set=canary --seed=2026 --max-batch=16 --report json`

Maya: rerun results: median back to within 1% of baseline, p99 down to baseline levels. Looks like batch size heuristics pushed us into inefficient kernel on synthetic flow.

Ravi: so two vectors: kernel selector weight change made matmul_kernel_v2 preferred for certain batch/seq combos, and batching heuristics sometimes exceed the knee point. Fix options: revert 3421, or make selector consider batch_size*seq_length product, or clamp batch size in the heuristic.

Sandeep: we should also verify KV cache change isn't contributing to replay tail spikes — I'll run the replay with KV eviction disabled to confirm.

Jen: quick patch idea: change selector to prefer matmul_kernel_fast when batch_size <= 16 or when batch_size*seq <= 8192. Small change, low risk. I'll open a draft PR.

Alex: can we avoid a noisy CI alert for this class of regression? This was a deterministic regression triggered by a small change, but sometimes noise causes one-off alerts. I propose CI only pages after 3 consecutive nightly-failures or add a secondary comparison using replay harness before alerting.

CI-bot: suggested CI policy update recorded at https://go.redwood/policies/bench-ci#proposal-5 — "require 3 consecutive nightly deviations or a replay-confirmed deviation before creating an incident".

Kai: For now, set the nightly alerting to hold for 48h or require replay confirmation. Also add per-model thresholds that account for natural variance at long sequences.

Maya: I ran the replay with KV eviction disabled — tail spikes went away. So KV change contributed to some of the replay variance, but synthetic median reg is mostly kernel/batching related.

Alex: action items: (1) Jen to open PR adjusting selector to include batch*seq guard (assign Jen), (2) Ravi to review and if acceptable we ship quick revert patch for 3421 if needed, (3) Sandeep to run KV-disabled replay baseline and post results to #perf-dash, (4) Kai to update CI alerting rules to require replay confirmation or 3 consecutive fails.

Jen: PR draft opened: https://git.redwood/infer/runtime/pulls/3449 — patch adjusts selector and adds unit test.

Ravi: I'll review 3449 today. If green, we can merge and schedule a small canary rollout to dedicated pool.

bench-bot: re-run scheduled: synthetic + replay canary in 30m. Will post results.

Maya: thanks all. I'll monitor the canary and mark the nightly alert as triaged for now. If the canary shows improvement we'll close INF-879.

Alex: marking this thread resolved for triage. Follow-ups tracked in INF-879 and PR#3449. Sandeep will keep an eye on the next 3 nightlies. :thumbsup:

Sandeep: will watch and report back tomorrow morning with the 00:00 UTC results.

CI-bot: canary finished — synthetic median delta now +0.6%, replay p99 within baseline. Closing auto-ticket pending human confirm.

Alex: great, thanks everyone. We'll loop back if anything reappears.
